samples.question: The image shows one opaque light-gray square chip on a plain white background, together with scattered gray bars that all lie outside the chip. Inside the chip, one network of thick dark corridors of constant width joins six small square markers. Three markers sit inside the chip and are coloured, one orange, one purple and one blue; each of those three sits where exactly three corridors meet. Two markers are green and one marker is yellow, and all three of those sit on the chip's border. Every corridor either joins two markers or runs from one marker to the chip's border and stops there; no two corridors cross or touch except at a marker, and between any two markers there is exactly one route along corridors that never reuses a corridor. From each green marker take that one route to the yellow marker. The two routes begin apart and then run together, and the first marker that both routes pass through is always one of the three coloured markers. The gray bars outside the chip are decoration and mean nothing. Which coloured marker is the first marker that both routes pass through? Answer orange, purple or blue.
